original_question: Determine whether there exist II1 factors N and M such that N is strongly solid, M contains an existential copy of N, and M nevertheless admits a Cartan subalgebra.
target_in_paper: Section Existential embeddings, Problem 8. This is the paper’s matching official open problem: whether there are II1 factors N and M with N strongly solid, M containing an existential copy of N, and M admitting a Cartan subalgebra. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2511.20377v1))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper very closely: it has the right ambient objects (II1 factors), the right asymmetry between N and M, the right model-theoretic relation (M contains an existential copy of N), and the right conclusion to test (M admits a Cartan subalgebra). In substance, it is essentially Problem 8. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2511.20377v1))
missing_details: The paper’s official formulation is an open problem labeled Problem 8 in the section Existential embeddings; identifying that label makes the target precise and avoids drifting to neighboring problems such as the surface-group question in Problem 9. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2511.20377v1))

To make the question stand-alone, “M contains an existential copy of N” should be unpacked: there should exist a unital trace-preserving *-embedding i:N→M such that, for some nonprincipal ultrafilter U on ℕ, there is a unital trace-preserving *-embedding j:M→N^U with j∘i equal to the diagonal embedding of N into its tracial ultrapower N^U. The section introduction recalls this notion. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2511.20377v1))

The ambient framework is the tracial/II1-factor setting with tracial ultrapowers; this is fixed in the opening conventions after the abstract and should be made explicit if the question is to stand alone. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2511.20377v1))
The note leaves standard operator-algebraic terminology implicit here, so a self-contained rewrite should spell out what “strongly solid” means and what a “Cartan subalgebra” means.

No extra hypotheses such as separability, Connes embeddability, group-factor origin, hyperbolicity, or surface-group assumptions belong to Problem 8 as stated; adding them would broaden or shift the problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2511.20377v1))
refined_question: Do there exist II1 factors N and M and a unital trace-preserving *-embedding i:N→M such that: (1) N is strongly solid, meaning that for every diffuse amenable von Neumann subalgebra A⊂N, the von Neumann algebra generated by the normalizer of A in N is amenable; (2) i is existential, in the sense that for some nonprincipal ultrafilter U on ℕ there exists a unital trace-preserving *-embedding j:M→N^U with j∘i equal to the diagonal embedding N→N^U; and (3) M admits a Cartan subalgebra, i.e. a maximal abelian self-adjoint subalgebra whose normalizer generates M? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2511.20377v1))
justification: The draft is already almost verbatim the paper’s Problem 8, so the only real refinement needed is to make the model-theoretic phrase “contains an existential copy” explicit using the paper’s recalled ultrapower-based definition, and to expand the standard operator-algebraic terms so that the result is self-contained. The opening paragraph supplies the ambient ultrapower notation and II1-factor context, and the Existential embeddings section immediately before Problem 8 supplies the definition of existential embedding. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2511.20377v1))
